title: PowerToys has detected an app... Always On Top message
author: TheAssurer2009
summary: Always On Top warns about an elevated foreground application but discards the foreground window identity, so the toast never says which application triggered it.

status.label: Medium-confidence Always On Top fix design
status.detail: Add filename-safe identity lookup from the foreground HWND and format it into the existing elevation warning, with bounded title and generic fallbacks.

next_action.label: Approve the forked fix design
next_action.reason: The exact warning call site and static resource are confirmed; implementation remains gated on design approval.

judgment.rationale: The issue's screenshots and discussion show a static elevation warning without an application name. Current Always On Top code receives the foreground HWND, checks only a boolean elevation result, and sends an unformatted resource string. A focused identity lookup and message-template change is implementation-ready, with fallbacks for protected or short-lived windows.
evidence: Issue report expects the particular application to be identified and says the notification appears at logon, sometimes twice.
Two attached screenshots show the static AlwaysOnTop toast with no application name.
AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent handles EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND and passes IDS_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND_ELEVATED unchanged.
IsProcessOfWindowElevated resolves the foreground HWND to a PID only to return TokenIsElevated.
NotificationUtil::WarnIfElevationIsRequired displays the supplied message and suppresses later warnings per module instance.
No active linked fix, assignee, or fork mirror existed before this run; the historical duplicate target is closed.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the mirror design, then hand off to the design-to-PR workflow; do not post upstream changes from this artifact.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete upstream or fork-side implementation covers the missing application identity. The repository-local call path supports a focused fix without changing shared notification suppression or activation behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Name the elevated foreground application in the Always On Top warning
proposed_fixes.root_cause: AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent receives the foreground HWND but reduces it to a boolean elevation check, then sends a static resource message to NotificationUtil; process identity is therefore lost before the toast is created.
plan: Add an additive limited-information image-path helper beside IsProcessOfWindowElevated in src/common/utils/elevation.h, returning an empty result for invalid, inaccessible, or raced processes.
In AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent, derive only the executable filename from the elevated foreground HWND, with a bounded window-title and generic fallback when image lookup is unavailable.

Add a localized formatted resource template in Resources.resx and pass the formatted message through the existing NotificationUtil::WarnIfElevationIsRequired API; preserve m_warningShown, actions, and elevation gating.
Add focused common-helper safety tests and validate the native Always On Top build plus a manual elevated-window toast scenario.
verification: Run PowerToys unelevated, foreground elevated Task Scheduler or Task Manager, and confirm the toast names the executable or safe title fallback.
Confirm normal non-elevated foreground changes do not show the warning and normal pin/unpin behavior remains unchanged.
Confirm protected or destroyed windows produce a generic safe message rather than a failure or full path.

confidence.rationale: The missing identity is directly confirmed by screenshots and the exact call site; protected/UWP windows may deny image-path access, so fallback behavior must be tested.

issue_context.summary: Users receive an Always On Top elevation warning but cannot tell which application triggered it; reports include logon, Task Scheduler, and post-Outlook pinning scenarios.
known_information: The report is for PowerToys 0.77.0 on Windows 11 Pro and says PowerToys is running as administrator.
The warning body is static and contains no process or window identity.
The foreground event handler has the triggering HWND and calls IsProcessOfWindowElevated.
The shared notification utility accepts a caller-supplied message and suppresses repeated warnings per instance.
The discussion requests application identity, an ignore option, and a specific disable control.
Two screenshots were retrieved and both show the same unnamed AlwaysOnTop toast.
inferences: The primary defect is loss of identity at the Always On Top call site, not toast rendering.
The first qualifying foreground event may be a shell or protected window, so identity lookup must have safe fallbacks.

Duplicate appearances can involve multiple qualifying foreground notifications or module instances; naming the triggering window is the directly supported scope, while suppression semantics should remain unchanged.
issue_context.analysis: The code path is sufficiently concrete for a design: the foreground HWND is available exactly where the warning is raised, and Windows permits a limited-information image-name query in more cases than a full process query. The design avoids exposing full paths and keeps common notification policy stable.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, all 23 comments, issue events, and the two attached screenshots.
Inspected AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent, NotificationUtil::WarnIfElevationIsRequired, IsProcessOfWindowElevated, process-path helpers, and the existing elevation unit tests.
Reviewed the history that introduced the Always On Top warning (commit cd57659ef) and found no later fix for application identity.
Checked MuyuanMS/PowerToys for an existing mirror and found none before creating fork issue 629.

information_gaps.information: Whether the first logon foreground event is always a real application window or sometimes a shell/protected window.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether implementation should filter non-application HWNDs or rely on the generic fallback without suppressing a legitimate warning.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: During manual verification, record the foreground executable/title at logon and when opening Task Scheduler; do not include full local paths in public artifacts.

design.root_cause: AlwaysOnTop::HandleWinHookEvent receives the foreground HWND but only uses it for a boolean elevation test; the process identity is discarded before NotificationUtil creates a static unnamed toast.
evidence: Observed: the two screenshots show the same static message with no application identity.
Observed: AlwaysOnTop.cpp lines 808-818 call IsProcessOfWindowElevated(data->hwnd) and pass IDS_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND_ELEVATED unchanged.
Observed: elevation.h lines 545-570 resolve a PID and return TokenIsElevated without returning the PID or image path.
Observed: NotificationUtil.cpp lines 33-48 displays the caller message and sets m_warningShown.
Inferred: adding identity extraction at the existing foreground-event boundary fixes the missing information without changing toast policy.

affected_files.purpose: Processes foreground accessibility events and raises the elevation warning.
Owns Always On Top state; optional declaration for a testable name-selection helper.
Neutral localized strings for the elevation toast.
Elevation and limited-information process identity helpers.
Existing Always On Top UI test location; extend only if notification text is observable deterministically.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The existing helper checks the HWND's process token but exposes only a boolean result.
implementation_steps.change: Add an additive helper using GetWindowThreadProcessId, OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), and QueryFullProcessImageNameW; return an empty string for invalid or inaccessible windows.
implementation_steps.code_block: inline std::wstring GetProcessImageNameOfWindow(HWND window) noexcept { DWORD pid{}; if (!window || !GetWindowThreadProcessId(window, &pid) || !pid) return {}; wil::unique_handle process{ OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, pid) }; if (!process) return {}; wchar_t path[...]; DWORD length = ARRAYSIZE(path); return QueryFullProcessImageNameW(process.get(), 0, path, &length) ? std::wstring(path, length) : std::wstring{}; }
edge_cases: Foreground HWND may be destroyed between PID and process-open calls.
Protected processes may deny the query.
Do not require VM_READ or expose command-line arguments.
tests: Desktop window returns either a path or empty result without crashing.
Current-process path may be asserted only through a reliable test window seam.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Every elevated foreground event sends a static generic message.
implementation_steps.change: For the already-elevated branch, resolve the filename from the foreground HWND, fall back to a bounded window title, then to a neutral generic label; format the message and call the existing notification utility.
implementation_steps.code_block: const auto path = GetProcessImageNameOfWindow(data->hwnd); const auto name = FileNameOrBoundedTitleOrFallback(path, data->hwnd); const auto message = fmt::format(GET_RESOURCE_STRING(IDS_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND_ELEVATED_WITH_NAME), name); m_notificationUtil->WarnIfElevationIsRequired(title, message, learnMore, dontShowAgain);
edge_cases: Strip directory components and never display a full path.
Bound title length and tolerate empty/destroyed HWND.
Keep !is_process_elevated(), m_warningShown, actions, and hook threading unchanged.
tests: Unit-test pure filename/fallback selection if extracted.
Manual elevated Task Scheduler/Task Manager verification.
Manual regression for ordinary non-elevated foreground and pin/unpin.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Only the generic static message is defined.
implementation_steps.change: Add a localized format template such as `We've detected "{}" running with administrator privileges. This will prevent certain interactions with this application.` and regenerate resource headers through the normal build.
implementation_steps.code_block: <data name="System_Foreground_Elevated_With_Name"><value>We've detected "{}" running with administrator privileges. This will prevent certain interactions with this application.</value></data>
edge_cases: Keep the existing generic resource as a fallback.
Use the repository's existing fmt formatting convention.
Do not hand-edit generated resource output.
tests: Confirm the generated resource identifier builds and the toast includes the executable filename.

implementation_steps.change: Add focused helper safety coverage and use the existing UI test project only if notification text can be observed reliably; otherwise document the manual end-to-end validation.

verify: Discover and use the existing repository build configuration for the Always On Top native project and common unit tests.
Run the targeted elevation tests with Visual Studio Test Explorer or vstest.console.exe per repository guidance.
Run PowerToys unelevated, foreground an elevated Task Scheduler or Task Manager window, and verify the toast names the executable or safe title fallback.
Verify no warning for ordinary non-elevated windows, existing Learn more and Don't show again actions remain, and Always On Top pin/unpin behavior is unchanged.
Exercise a protected or short-lived foreground window and verify safe generic fallback without a crash or full path disclosure.
risks: Process identity can race with window destruction or be denied for protected processes; mitigate with empty-result fallbacks.
Window titles may contain sensitive or misleading text; use executable filename first, bound the title fallback, and never expose a full path.
Resource formatting and generated headers can affect localization/build output; regenerate through the normal project build.
The shared elevation header is used by other modules; keep the helper additive and preserve IsProcessOfWindowElevated semantics.
alternatives: Change only the static English message: rejected because it cannot identify the triggering application.
Move process enumeration into NotificationUtil: rejected because it loses the precise foreground HWND and broadens unrelated callers.
Show the full executable path: rejected because it leaks unnecessary local path information.
Enumerate every elevated process: rejected because the warning concerns the foreground window and would create false positives.
